reasons.reproducibility: Desk life-cycle calculation of water footprint; repeatable with published data.
reasons.effectiveness: Reports no algae or water-quality data; shade-ball algae control is called an open question.
reasons.cost: A desk analysis costs little beyond reference data.
reasons.time: Payback of 0.2-2.5 years is a calculation; no algae result.
reasons.environment: 96 million HDPE balls cost 0.25-2.9 million m3 of water to make and become plastic waste.

reasons.reproducibility: Review; the cited pool test (covered vs uncovered pools) could be copied with a sponsor.
reasons.effectiveness: Algae evidence is second-hand plus one unreplicated unpublished pool test measured by turbidity, not algal counts.
reasons.cost: Shade balls or cloth for small pools cost about $150-500.
reasons.time: The pool test compared water over June-September, but differences show within weeks.
reasons.environment: Polyethylene objects leave recalcitrant residues, possible leachates and microplastics.

reasons.reproducibility: Suspended shade-cloth cover over a 2,400 m2 irrigation reservoir; not school-repeatable.
reasons.effectiveness: Algal growth 'highly limited' under the cover, but one reservoir before/after with Chl a shown only in a figure and a farmer-reported 90% filter benefit.
reasons.cost: Cover costs EUR 7.80/m2, about EUR 19,000 for the reservoir.
reasons.time: Compared an uncovered year with a covered year.
reasons.environment: Near-total light removal stops all photosynthesis; cover material is durable but removable.

reasons.reproducibility: Randomized trial in six 0.05 ha catfish ponds; needs aquaculture ponds.
reasons.effectiveness: Chl a did not differ significantly (late season 117 vs 208 ug/L, P=0.14) and odorous cyanobacteria occurred in all six ponds.
reasons.cost: Six production ponds with fish over a season cost far over $5,000.
reasons.time: Monthly dye doses June-September, judged at October harvest.
reasons.environment: Dye half-disappeared in ~10 days; no change in ammonia, nitrite or aeration.

reasons.reproducibility: Randomized trial in nine fertilized 0.04 ha fish ponds; needs aquaculture facilities.
reasons.effectiveness: Opposite effect: mean Chl a was significantly higher in dyed ponds (86.5 and 75.5 vs 66.7 ug/L, P=0.02) and cyanobacteria unchanged.
reasons.cost: Nine stocked production ponds cost far over $5,000.
reasons.environment: Dye at 2.4x label rate showed no significant water-quality or fish harm; short-lived residue.

reasons.reproducibility: Six catfish ponds treated from April to August.
reasons.effectiveness: Chlorophyll-a and weed cover did not differ from controls and Secchi depth barely changed.
reasons.environment: Dusk dissolved oxygen was lower in treated ponds, and dye persisted, fading ~0.75 mg/L per month.

reasons.reproducibility: 3-m deep outdoor tanks with reservoir water and light meters; a scaled-down version is possible but the tanks are specialist.
reasons.effectiveness: Algae were not measured; only transparency fell ~10-30%, and 1 mg/L had no significant effect with clay turbidity.
reasons.cost: Deep tanks and an underwater light sensor likely $500-5,000.
reasons.environment: Dye residue added; visibility stays above swimming standards at label rates.

reasons.reproducibility: A 0.95 ha, 1 MWp floating solar array on a drinking-water reservoir; industrial scale.
reasons.effectiveness: Plankton barely changed, and benthic cyanobacterial mats appeared under the array.
reasons.cost: Floating PV installation costs far over $5,000.
reasons.environment: Benthic mats made geosmin up to 20 ng/L, anatoxin-a and microcystins; Chara disappeared under the array.

reasons.reproducibility: 40% floating PV cover on 800-3,000 m2 aquaculture ponds at three institutes; not school-repeatable.
reasons.effectiveness: Plankton biomass ~61-68% lower under FPV, but one pond per treatment per site (pseudoreplicated sampling).
reasons.cost: Floating PV buoys on ponds cost far over $5,000.
reasons.time: Compared over a full culture season.
reasons.environment: FPV ponds had significantly higher ammonia and orthophosphate at some sites.

reasons.reproducibility: 1-D MyLake-FPV model runs; needs specialist modelling skills and reservoir data.
reasons.effectiveness: Modelled only, with assumed wind/light effects; big Chl a cuts only at high cover and slow-tank siting could raise Chl a up to 4%.
reasons.cost: Model software is free but site data and setup take specialist time.
reasons.time: A real FPV effect on peak chlorophyll would take a growing season to appear, not days.
reasons.environment: Modelled cooling and possible shade-tolerant species shifts.

reasons.reproducibility: 3-D ELCD model plus field sensors on a reservoir demo; specialist tools.
reasons.effectiveness: The 30% Chl a cut under panels is purely modelled; the 1 ha demo measured no chlorophyll.
reasons.cost: Modelling and sonde data collection cost roughly $150-500 to repeat.
reasons.time: A real change under FPV would take a season to show.
reasons.environment: Model predicts DO down up to 50% and TP up 30% under panels.

reasons.reproducibility: Needs purchased P. rubescens strains and single-filament picking under a microscope.
reasons.effectiveness: Darkness killed filaments slowly and unevenly: 0% to >50% viable at 58 days, and the hardiest strain needed 111 days.
reasons.cost: Strains, tubes and a cold incubator cost about $150-500.
reasons.time: Viability differences took about two months (50% mortality ~70 days).
reasons.environment: Darkness adds nothing to the water.
